topic: Unique traffic calculation and session recalibration
summary_markdown:
The discussion focused on how Unique Traffic is calculated, particularly when data is reaggregated or calibrated. It was confirmed that if the session calibration process (updating `is_calibrated`) changes based on a new signal level, the resulting Unique Traffic will change, even if the Total Traffic remains constant.

To address this, modifications were made to the aggregation template in Data Science. The goal is to allow for staging environment testing and historical recalculation without needing to recalibrate all sessions during every refresh. Instead of relying solely on the `is_calibrated` field, a function `isCalibrated(company_num, facility_num, session_start_hour, is_prod, signal_level, session_duration)` will be used for calibration checks.

This new approach allows for refreshing dictionaries in the CH and recalculating the model and historical data by running a job, which should only require full session recalibration upon official release.
decisions: The Unique Traffic metric is expected to change when sessions are re-calibrated using a new signal level.
A new aggregation template was developed to allow for staging environment testing and historical data recalculation without mandatory session recalibration.
